title: Fruits
summary: Discover 125 fruits, from familiar favorites to rare regional treasures, through weight, flavor, growing regions and surprising facts.
dataNote: Whole-fruit examples in grams, including natural peel, shell and seeds unless noted. A source may report a range, cultivar or sample mean. Chosen examples are not species averages or record comparisons. Undocumented weights are null and excluded from arithmetic. Burrow editorial ratings from 1 to 10, interpreting descriptions of ripe fruit: 1 barely sweet/tart, 5 moderate, 10 very sweet/tart. Not Brix, sugar grams, laboratory acidity, health scores or tastiness judgments. Breadfruit is rated at the mature cooking stage, plantain ripe and cooked, and olive after curing; weights remain whole fruits before cooking or curing. Cultivar, ripeness and personal perception change flavor. Burrow editorial findability bands, 1 to 5, for fresh fruit beyond its home region: 1 local harvest/specialist growers; 2 mostly regional/seasonal; 3 specialty markets; 4 regional staple traded abroad; 5 widely traded. Not a country count, current store inventory, conservation status or price. Based on described cultivation and trade, with no implied worldwide census. Origin or cultural/cultivation association, not an exhaustive distribution. Map pins mark representative places within the stated region, not a precisely known birthplace. Ancient origins and some species boundaries remain debated. Individually credited Commons photos. Stored as resized JPEGs for offline play; no botanical drawings or generated substitutes. Fruit cards include distinct species and familiar market types or cultivar groups, such as nectarines, satsumas and golden kiwifruit; the card count is not a count of unique species.
